# dsh-mcp-summon
English | 中文
Dormant-by-default MCP for DeepSeek Harness: MCP servers cost nothing until the model **summons** on
e — and what arrives is not a proxy, it is the server's **real native tools**.
## The problem
The official bridge (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`) connects every configured server at startup and
registers **every** tool as a native tool, so every JSON schema enters **every model request forever
** — whether the model ever calls them or not. A fat server pays that toll on every single turn:

| Server | Tools | Schema bytes | ≈ tokens / turn |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| xerj (published s

chema, measured 2026-10-28) | 22 | 53,297 | **13,325** |
| chrome-devtools-mcp (measured by dsh-mcp-

lazy) | 29 | 21,252 | 5,313 |
| this repo's test fixture | 5 | 902 | 226 |
## What you get
At load the plugin registers exactly **one** tool, `mcp_summon`, whose description carries a card pe
r configured server — capability summary, tool count, and an honest cost line measured the same way

After a summon the tools are **real native tools** — the same `ToolDefinition` adapter the official
bridge uses (vendored, MIT notice reproduced): real schemas, native UI rendering, per-tool approval
gates, image results admitted to durable storage intact. The harness re-assembles the tool set every
turn, so they appear from the next turn and behave exactly like normally bridged MCP tools.
A crash or profile restart falls back to dormant-by-default — the safe direction. Session end releas
file restart falls back to dormant-by-default — the safe direction. Session end releases everything.

Restart the profile. Servers stay dormant until summoned — nothing spawns at load.

## How it works
| Mechanism | dsh seam |
| One tool at load, zero processes | `ctx.tools.register` in `apply`; the only startup I/O is one re

ad of the measurement cache |
| Daemon-backed servers | probe `healthUrl` → spawn detached + unref'd

→ poll until healthy → connect the proxy; `release` leaves the daemon running |
| Summoned tools ap
pear next turn | `register` fires `tools/change` — "a global change concerns every agent's next asse

mbly" — and the tool set is re-assembled per turn |
| Real native behaviour | the official bridge's
tool adapter, transport factory and naming rule vendored from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` 0.2.1-rc

.3 (MIT) |
| Honest cost lines | JSON bytes of `{name, description, parameters}` ÷ 4 — exactly the f

ields the registry's `schemas()` whitelists onto the wire |
| Byte-stable cards | sorted by `serverN
ame`, frozen for the session; a fresh measurement lands in the **next** session's cards from `$DSH_H

OME/storages/dsh-mcp-summon/cache.json` — a server is never spawned just to card it |
| Release | th

e exact disposers `ctx.tools.register` returned, then `transport.close()` kills the child |
| Crash
| `onclose` → unregister → dormant, reason kept for `status` |
Activating a server changes the tool block once, so that turn's prompt-cache prefix is invalidated o
nce — that is the documented price of activation, and it is paid whether you summon or the official
bridge registers at startup.

## Known limitations
The v1 boundary, stated plainly:

- **stdio only.** No `streamable-http` rows yet.
- **Tools only.** No MCP resources, prompts, sampli

ng or elicitation.
- **No OAuth.** Auth is whatever the row's `env` can carry.
- **No idle reclamati

on.** A summoned server stays until you release it or the session ends.
- **No reconnect with backof

f.** A crashed server goes dormant with the reason in `status`; re-summon to retry.
- **Cards are fr
ozen within a session.** A first summon's measurement shows up in the next session's cards (mid-sess

ion numbers are one `status` call away).
- **A secret passed through `args` lands in argv**, readabl

e by `ps`; `env` is the safe path.
- **`mcp_summon`'s own description is a permanent cost** (~400 to
kens with two servers) — the floor this plugin pays so the model can decide to activate anything at
with two servers) — the floor this plugin pays so the model can decide to activate anything at all.
